newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's unions to present new labour reform ideas.
newsitem.headline: Spain's unions to present new labour reform ideas.

text.p: Spain's major unions will present a new proposal to bridge some of the gaps with employers when labour reform talks resume on Wednesday.
The unions are offering to weaken conditions controlling dismissals in exchange for a new permanent contract.
The severance pay under the new contract would be in a band between 20 days per year worked, as proposed by the employers and 45 days as current legislation dictates.

"The severance pay has to be sufficiently far away from the current 45 days...for the employers to have some incentive to employ people on permanent contracts," said Candido Menendez, a leader of the UGT trade union said at a news conference.
"But it has to be sufficiently greater than 20 days to dissuade employers from firing."
The head of the Workers Commission Union, Antonio Gutierrez, said the proposal demonstrated the willingness of unions to "risk the maximum to defend people who are unemployed."
Talks between unions and employers came to a standstill last Thursday over disputes on youth contracts.
